sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Evolution**: The office of Peshwa was originally one of the **Ashta Pradhan** (Council of Eight) under Shivaji, but became hereditary and supreme under **Balaji Vishwanath** (1713-1720).
• **Sangola Agreement (1750)**: Formally transferred the executive power from the Chhatrapati to the Peshwa, making the Peshwa the de facto head of the Maratha state.
• **Confederacy Model**: The Maratha Empire evolved into a loose confederacy of powerful chiefs (Scindias, Holkars, Gaekwads, Bhonsles) under the nominal leadership of the Peshwa.
• **Key Metric**: The expansion of the 'Swarajya' to 'Samrajya' (Empire) through the collection of **Chauth** (1/4th revenue) and **Sardeshmukhi** (1/10th additional levy).

items.definition: Financial mechanisms used to extract revenue from non-Maratha territories; Chauth was for protection, Sardeshmukhi was a hereditary right.
A political structure where regional chiefs operated autonomously but acknowledged the Peshwa's authority in matters of national interest.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Military Strategy**: Use of light cavalry and guerrilla warfare (Ganimi Kava) evolved into large-scale artillery-based warfare by the mid-18th century.
• **Diplomatic Reach**: Extensive network of 'Vakils' (agents) in various princely courts to monitor political developments.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Lack of a unified central administration, internal rivalry among confederate chiefs, and financial strain from constant warfare.
• **Solutions**: Attempts at fiscal reform by Nana Phadnavis to stabilize the state after the 1761 disaster.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'B-B-B-M-B' (Balaji V, Baji Rao I, Balaji Baji, Madhav Rao, Baji Rao II).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Chronological order of the most significant Peshwas.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 'Ashta Pradhan' (Shivaji's council) with the 'Peshwa-led Confederacy'. Remember, the Peshwa was only one of the eight in Shivaji's time, not the ruler.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Decentralized Centralism' to describe the Maratha Confederacy under the Peshwas.

keyTakeaways: The Peshwas shifted the Maratha state from a centralized monarchy to a decentralized confederacy.
The Third Battle of Panipat (1761) was the turning point that halted Maratha expansion and exposed the fragility of the confederacy.
The Peshwa office ended with the Third Anglo-Maratha War (1817-1818) when Baji Rao II was deposed by the British.
